theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.loss_cNextProj_sub_loss
theorems.informal: Pathwise, for every noise realisation: L(x+) - L(x) = -eta * sum_{i in S} g_i lam_i c_i + (eta^2/2) * sum_{i in S} lam_i g_i^2 with g_i = lam_i c_i + zeta_i, i.e. Delta L = -eta g^T A x + (eta^2/2) g^T A g for the S-projected update.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.loss_cNextProj_sub_loss_eq_sum
theorems.informal: L(cNextProj S eta c zeta) - L(c) = sum_{i in S} (lam_i/2) (((1 - eta lam_i) c_i - eta zeta_i)^2 - c_i^2).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_eq_sum
theorems.informal: expLossChange = -eta s^S + (eta^2/2)(tau^S + n^loss_S) equals sum_{i in S} (lam_i/2) ((1 - eta lam_i)^2 c_i^2 + eta^2 kap2_i - c_i^2), the sum of per-coordinate expected loss changes.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.loss_cNextProj_sub_loss_eq_expLossChange_add
theorems.informal: Pathwise decomposition Delta L = expLossChange - eta sum_S lam_i (1 - eta lam_i) c_i zeta_i + (eta^2/2) sum_S lam_i (zeta_i^2 - kap2_i); the last two terms are mean-zero when E zeta_i = 0, E zeta_i^2 = kap2_i.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.weighted_sum_loss_change
theorems.informal: For finitely supported noise with weights summing to 1, mean 0 and second moments kap2_i on S, the weighted average of L(x+) - L(x) equals expLossChange.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_neg_iff
theorems.informal: If tau^S + n^loss_S > 0 then for every real eta: expLossChange N S eta c < 0 <-> 0 < eta and eta < etaLoss N S c. (eta > 0 is part of the iff; s^S > 0 is not needed.)

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.proj_loss_step_size_condition
theorems.informal: With both denominators positive: E Delta L_D < 0 <-> 0 < eta < etaLossD, and E Delta L_B < 0 <-> 0 < eta < etaLossB.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_neg_iff_of_pos
theorems.informal: If tau^S + n^loss_S > 0 and eta > 0: expLossChange < 0 <-> eta < etaLoss.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_pos_iff
theorems.informal: If tau^S + n^loss_S > 0: 0 < expLossChange <-> eta < 0 or etaLoss < eta.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_pos_iff_of_pos
theorems.informal: If tau^S + n^loss_S > 0 and eta > 0: 0 < expLossChange <-> etaLoss < eta.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_eq_zero_iff
theorems.informal: If tau^S + n^loss_S > 0: expLossChange = 0 <-> eta = 0 or eta = etaLoss; also expLossChange_eq_factor: expLossChange = ((tau^S+n^loss_S)/2) eta (eta - etaLoss).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_eq_zero_of_lossDen_eq_zero
theorems.informal: If tau^S + n^loss_S = 0 then expLossChange = 0 for all eta (threshold is 0/0 in the paper); companion: expLossChange_nonneg_of_mom_eq_zero (s^S = 0 implies E Delta L >= 0).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.alphaT_pos
theorems.informal: If s^D > 0 and s^B > 0 then alpha_t > 0; quantitatively gap_mul_s_le_alphaT: s_t (lam_k - lam_{k+1}) <= alpha_t, and alphaT_le: alpha_t <= s_t (lam_1 - lam_d).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.alphaT_zero
theorems.paperItem: Lemma crossover-quadratic-properties, item 1 ('for all x_t, alpha_t > 0')
theorems.informal: alpha_t = 0 at the state x_t = 0: formal counterexample to the literal 'for all x_t'.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.gammaT_neg
theorems.informal: If n^loss_D > 0 then gamma_t < 0 (gammaT_neg_iff: gamma_t < 0 <-> n^loss_D > 0; gammaT_nonpos unconditionally).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.hQuad_one
theorems.informal: h(1) = alpha_t + beta_t + gamma_t = n^loss_B and h(0) = gamma_t (hQuad_zero, hQuad_one_eq_sum).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.crossover_quadratic_properties
theorems.informal: Under s^D, s^B, n^loss_D, n^loss_B > 0: alpha_t > 0, gamma_t < 0, h(0) = gamma_t < 0, h(1) = alpha+beta+gamma > 0.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.crossover_critical_root
theorems.informal: Under s^D, s^B, n^loss_D, n^loss_B > 0: thetaCrit = (-beta + sqrt(beta^2 - 4 alpha gamma))/(2 alpha) lies in (0,1), h < 0 on (0, thetaCrit), h > 0 on (thetaCrit, 1), h(thetaCrit) = 0, and it is the only root of h in (0,1).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.hQuad_neg_iff
theorems.informal: If alpha_t > 0 then for every theta > 0: h(theta) < 0 <-> theta < thetaCrit; likewise hQuad_pos_iff (h > 0 <-> theta > thetaCrit) and hQuad_eq_zero_iff (h = 0 <-> theta = thetaCrit); hQuad_thetaCrit: h(thetaCrit) = 0.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.existsUnique_hQuad_root
theorems.informal: If alpha_t > 0, n^loss_D > 0, n^loss_B > 0 then there is a unique theta in (0,1) with h(theta) = 0 (namely thetaCrit; thetaCrit_mem_Ioo).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.thetaCrit_lt_one_iff
theorems.paperItem: Lemma critical-root (location of the root; sharpness of noise hypotheses)
theorems.informal: For alpha_t > 0: thetaCrit < 1 <-> n^loss_B > 0; thetaCrit_pos_iff: thetaCrit > 0 <-> n^loss_D > 0 or n^loss_B < alpha_t; always 0 <= thetaCrit <= 1; thetaCrit_eq_one / thetaCrit_eq_zero in the degenerate noise cases.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.lossGap_eq_s_mul_hQuad
theorems.informal: If s^D, s^B > 0: s^D (tau^B + n^loss_B) - s^B (tau^D + n^loss_D) = s_t * h(theta_t).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.etaLossD_sub_etaLossB
theorems.informal: If s^D, s^B > 0: etaLossD - etaLossB = 2 s_t h(theta_t) / ((tau^D + n^loss_D)(tau^B + n^loss_B)); hence sign(etaLossD - etaLossB) = sign h(theta_t) (etaLossD_lt_etaLossB_iff_hQuad_neg, etaLossB_lt_etaLossD_iff_hQuad_pos, etaLossD_eq_etaLossB_iff_hQuad_eq_zero).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.theta_lt_thetaCrit_iff
theorems.informal: If s^D > 0 and s^B > 0 (i.e. 0 < theta_t < 1): theta_t < thetaCrit <-> etaLossD < etaLossB. No noise hypothesis needed.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.thetaCrit_lt_theta_iff
theorems.informal: If s^D > 0 and s^B > 0: thetaCrit < theta_t <-> etaLossB < etaLossD.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.theta_eq_thetaCrit_iff
theorems.informal: If s^D > 0 and s^B > 0: theta_t = thetaCrit <-> etaLossD = etaLossB.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.loss_crossover
theorems.informal: If 0 < theta_t < 1, n^loss_D > 0, n^loss_B > 0: thetaCrit is in (0,1), is a root of h and the only root of h in (0,1); theta_t < thetaCrit <-> etaLossD < etaLossB; theta_t > thetaCrit <-> etaLossD > etaLossB; theta_t = thetaCrit <-> etaLossD = etaLossB.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.expLossChange_D_pos_B_neg
theorems.informal: If both denominators tau^S + n^loss_S are positive and etaLossD < eta < etaLossB then E Delta L_D > 0 and E Delta L_B < 0 (mirror: expLossChange_B_pos_D_neg).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.low_alignment_descent
theorems.paperItem: Theorem 11 + Summary consequence (explanation of Song et al.)
theorems.informal: If s^D, s^B > 0 and theta_t < thetaCrit then etaLossD < etaLossB and for every eta in (etaLossD, etaLossB): E Delta L_D > 0 and E Delta L_B < 0 (mirror: high_alignment_descent).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.exists_D_pos_B_neg_iff
theorems.informal: For s^D, s^B > 0: a positive step size with E Delta L_D > 0 and E Delta L_B < 0 exists iff theta_t < thetaCrit.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.etaLossD_lt_etaLossB_smul_iff
theorems.informal: For s^D, s^B > 0 and t != 0: etaLossD(t c) < etaLossB(t c) <-> n^loss_B theta - n^loss_D (1 - theta) < t^2 alpha theta (1 - theta); with theta_smul (theta scale-invariant), alphaT_smul (alpha scales as t^2), thetaCrit_congr, and etaLossD_lt_etaLossB_iff (square-root-free criterion).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.nLossD_div_lt_thetaCrit
theorems.paperItem: Theorem 11 (state-independent bound on the state-dependent threshold)
theorems.informal: If alpha_t > 0, n^loss_D > 0, n^loss_B > 0 then n^loss_D/(n^loss_D + n^loss_B) < thetaCrit (< 1).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.Spec.one_sub_thetaCrit_mul
theorems.informal: For alpha_t > 0: (1 - thetaCrit)(alpha thetaCrit + n^loss_B + n^loss_D) = n^loss_B; hence one_sub_thetaCrit_mul_alphaT_le: (1 - thetaCrit) alpha <= n^loss_B, and nLossB_le_one_sub_thetaCrit_mul: n^loss_B <= (1 - thetaCrit)(alpha + n^loss_B + n^loss_D).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.LossThreshold.state_dependence_example
theorems.informal: lam=(2,1), kap2=(1,1): states (1,1) and (1/2,1/2) both have theta = 4/5, but etaLossD < etaLossB for the first and etaLossB < etaLossD for the second; so thetaCrit(c') < 4/5 < thetaCrit(c).

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.LossThreshold.thetaCrit_eq_zero_example
theorems.paperItem: Lemma crossover-quadratic-properties item 2 / Theorem 11 ('gamma_t < 0 for all x_t', 'thetaCrit in (0,1)')
theorems.informal: lam=(2,1), c=(1,1), kap2=(0,5) (Sigma PSD, trace 5 > 0): gamma_t = 0 and thetaCrit = 0, not in (0,1). Companion thetaCrit_eq_one_example: kap2=(1,0) gives thetaCrit = 1.

theorems.name: SuspiciousAlignment.LossThreshold.loss_crossover_nonvacuous
theorems.paperItem: non-vacuity of Theorems 10-11 and the Summary consequence
theorems.informal: lam=(2,1), kap2=(1,1), c=(1,1) satisfies 0 < theta < 1, n^loss_D > 0, n^loss_B > 0; suspicious_window_example: etaLossD = 4/5 < 9/10 < 1 = etaLossB and at eta = 9/10, E Delta L_D > 0 > E Delta L_B.

paperIssues: Theorem 10: the threshold eta^loss_S = 2 s^S/(tau^S + n^loss_S) is 0/0 when the state and the noise both vanish on S; then E[Delta L] == 0 (Spec.expLossChange_eq_zero_of_lossDen_eq_zero). The iff needs tau^S + n^loss_S > 0 (added as hypothesis). It does NOT need s^S > 0 (if s^S = 0 < n^loss_S both sides are false, eta^loss = 0), and eta > 0 is part of the equivalence for arbitrary real eta. The paper's proof only argues the 'if' direction ('holds for 0 < eta < ...'); the restated theorem at tex 1477 carries the wrong title.

Lemma crossover-quadratic-properties item 1 claims alpha_t > 0 for ALL x_t (proof: 'for any x_t, s_t > 0'). False at x_t = 0 (alpha = 0, Spec.alphaT_zero) and undefined (mu^S(3,2) = 0/0) when s^D = 0 or s^B = 0, i.e. theta_t in {0,1}. Correct hypothesis: s^D > 0 and s^B > 0 (0 < theta_t < 1); then even alpha_t >= s_t (lam_k - lam_{k+1}). Typo at tex 1544: lam_j * (lam_j^3 c_j^2) should be lam_j * (lam_j^2 c_j^2).

Lemma item 2 claims gamma_t = -n^loss_D < 0 and h(1) = n^loss_B > 0 for every noise. These are extra assumptions, not implied by the paper's Sigma PSD, Tr Sigma > 0. Formal counterexamples (lam=(2,1), c=(1,1)): kap2=(0,5) gives gamma_t = 0 and thetaCrit = 0; kap2=(1,0) gives h(1) = 0 and thetaCrit = 1. Precisely (alpha_t > 0): thetaCrit < 1 <-> n^loss_B > 0; thetaCrit > 0 <-> n^loss_D > 0 or n^loss_B < alpha_t. Hence 'thetaCrit in (0,1)' in Theorem 11 and the second lemma needs n^loss_D > 0 and n^loss_B > 0 (true if Sigma is positive definite).

Theorem 11: the two equivalences are correct for a fixed state with 0 < theta_t < 1 (and need no noise hypothesis), but the paper states them 'for a given x_t' without excluding theta_t in {0,1} (coefficients 0/0) or x_t = 0 (where, with theta(0)=0 and alpha=0, h has root n_D/(n_D+n_B) in (0,1) yet eta^loss_D = eta^loss_B = 0, so the first iff fails). The second lemma's 'critical function thetaCrit: R^d -> (0,1)' is only defined on {0 < theta(x) < 1}; the Summary's regime '[0, thetaCrit)' should be '(0, thetaCrit)'.

Theorem 11: thetaCrit_t is state-dependent (through alpha_t = s_t(mu^D(3,2) - mu^B(3,2))), not a universal threshold on the alignment. theta is scale-invariant while alpha scales like t^2 and n^loss does not scale: eta^loss_D(tx) < eta^loss_B(tx) <-> n_B theta - n_D(1-theta) < t^2 alpha theta (1-theta). Formal instance: lam=(2,1), kap2=(1,1), c=(1,1) and c'=(1/2,1/2) both have theta=4/5 but opposite threshold orderings. Only n_D/(n_D+n_B) < thetaCrit < 1 holds uniformly.

Proof of Theorem 11, typos: tex 1690 'u_t^B' should be tau_t^B; tex 1694 the sign identity reads s^D(u^B+n_B) - s^D(u^D+n_D) and should be s^D(tau^B+n_B) - s^B(tau^D+n_D); tex 1709 the coefficient of theta_t is printed as s_t(mu^D-mu^B)+n_B+n_D but must be -s_t(mu^D-mu^B)+n_B+n_D (= beta_t). The final alpha, beta, gamma and the identity numerator = s_t h(theta_t) are correct (verified).

Summary consequence (tex 619-626): 'for eta in (eta^loss_D, eta^loss_B): E Delta L_D > 0' needs tau^D + n^loss_D > 0; if s^D = 0 and n^loss_D = 0 then E Delta L_D == 0. Both denominators are automatically positive when 0 < theta_t < 1.
'Additional Notion' says alpha, beta, gamma all depend on x_t; gamma_t = -n^loss_D does not.

Heads-up outside this file's scope (Theorem 13, not formalized here, checked numerically only): the lower bound n_B/(s_t lam_{k+1}(m-1) + n_B + n_D) <= 1 - thetaCrit appears false in general, since alpha_t >= s_t lam_{k+1}(m-1) with strict inequality possible. Example: lam=(10,2,1), D={1,2}, c=(1,0,1), kap2=(1,1,1): alpha=909, s lam_{k+1}(m-1)=101, 1-thetaCrit ~ 0.001086 < 1/114 ~ 0.00877. The correct bounds proved here are n_B/(alpha+n_B+n_D) <= 1 - thetaCrit <= n_B/alpha (so the paper's upper bound holds).

- Theorem 10: only `0 < P.mom S 3 c + P.nLoss N S`; eta is an arbitrary real.
- alpha_t > 0: `0 < P.sD c` and `0 < P.sB c` (equivalent to 0 < theta < 1, `LossThreshold.theta_mem_Ioo_iff`).
- Theorem 11 equivalences: only s^D, s^B > 0. thetaCrit in (0,1): additionally `0 < P.nLossD N`, `0 < P.nLossB N` (both follow from `0 < N.smin` via `LossThreshold.nLossD_pos_of_smin_pos` / `nLossB_pos_of_smin_pos`).

Generic helpers (moments, nLoss, theta, mu bounds, abstract quadratic `LossThreshold.root`, the Fin 2 instances `spec2`, `noise2`, `noise11`) live in `SuspiciousAlignment.LossThreshold` with `P` explicit, e.g. `LossThreshold.theta_pos P hD`. Downstream files that `open LossThreshold` together with `open OneStep` will get ambiguous short names and should qualify them.
